current_difficulty_reason: A Lipschitz field of affine planes does not form a foliation to which the usual Lebesgue density theorem can simply be applied. Sections5–7 construct two rectifiable fibrations and quantitative coarea Jacobian bounds, then select transverse balls whose nonlinear stripes remain disjoint. The resulting near-full-volume lower bound closes the Section8 contradiction with the exact dimensional density constant after standard measure-theoretic foundations are allowed.
